name: A barrage of pokes climbs to one fed-up face, not one per poke
case: The person pokes Boop four times in a row, and each tap cuts short the face Boop is making, then keeps poking a second later. Boop's mood steps once at the first barrage (engaged, curious or uneasy), and it doesn't make its face again for the pokes that keep coming right after: its face for them is still in progress, even though a tap cut it short. At most three faces in all: a curious or glad one at the first poke, a miffed one at the second, then the fed-up one.
why: The one mood graph (2026-10-15): a mood moves one step along its pack's moves and holds at least 30 s (MoodPolicy), so a barrage moves the mood once. PERSONALITY's Examples: one poke gets a curious face, two in a row an annoyed one, three an irritated or grumpy one. A reaction a tap cut short stays in progress while the pokes go on, and a poke doesn't wake the brain while the reaction to its run's third or later poke is in progress with the mood unchanged. The first step checks its last pass; the second wakes nothing, so the run check counts the faces
